summary: The ENFORCE Act amends federal law to broaden prohibited conduct and increase criminal penalties for child pornography offenses involving adapted or modified depictions of identifiable minors. It also expands federal enforcement, removes statutes of limitations, updates sex offender registration requirements, restricts the reproduction of certain visual depictions in court discovery, adds pretrial detention presumptions, and mandates supervised release for offenses involving obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to increased criminal penalties, removal of the statute of limitations, mandatory sex offender registration, pretrial detention presumptions, and mandatory supervised release after imprisonment.
affected_groups.group: Individuals committing federal offenses related to child pornography or obscene visual representations of child sexual a

affected_groups.effect: Granted specific access rights to the visual depictions involving them during criminal proceedings, mirroring existing protections.
affected_groups.group: Identifiable minors depicted in visual representations or child pornography

key_provisions: Broadens the scope of prohibited conduct and updates penalties for producing child pornography involving adapted or modified depictions of an identifiable minor tied to interstate commerce.
Removes the statute of limitations for federal crimes involving obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse under section 1466A.
Updates sex offender registration requirements to include crimes involving obscene visual representations of child sexual abuse.
Prohibits the reproduction of visual depictions of child sexual abuse in criminal discovery, keeping them under the care, custody, and control of the government or court.
Establishes a presumption of detention pending trial for individuals charged with offenses under section 1466A(a).
Adds supervised release requirements following imprisonment for violations of section 1466A.
